name: manual_ad1dc8
claim: When hardening an address or endpoint denylist, add the sibling prefix classes as a set and then verify parity across every layer that dials, because the same class of gap usually exists on more than one side. Concretely: Teredo, 6to4, 6to4 relay anycast, CGNAT, loopback, ULA and link-local travel together, and a fix that lands in only one of the two sibling implementations leaves the other exploitable. Where the two layers sit on opposite sides of a regime boundary, reimplement the rules natively rather than importing across it, and prove parity with matching classification tests on both sides.

decisions.notes: The v2 gateway dialer already rejected Teredo and 6to4-encoded addresses but still allowed the 6to4 relay anycast prefix, which is shared infrastructure any attacker-adjacent network can answer on. The fix was committed in the oramasys dialer, and the v1 PT launcher needed the same rules reimplemented natively because PT must never import a v2 package; both sides ended up carrying matching classification tests. The wider lesson is that a denylist gap found on one layer is a strong signal to audit the sibling layer immediately instead of waiting for it to be reported separately.
